title: Console/Observability triage scratchpad - Nick Hernandez
content:
2026-03-04 // quick triage scratchpad

Summary: Customer (Acme Payments) reports missing panels and intermittent 500s on the Console > Observability > Model Latency dashboard. Initial contact from CSM via JIRA-4782. Customer says issue started ~2026-03-03 09:00 PST after a model rollout. They saw panels blank and some requests returning 500 with 'query_timeout' message.

Immediate notes / reproduce attempts:
- Looked at dashboard in prod (me, 2026-03-03 11:15 PST) - some panels load, others show 'no data' and a few error tiles with 500.
- Reproduced by switching to customer org (Acme) - same behavior for me in EU region.
- Checked traceIDs provided by customer: trace-01 and trace-02. Trace 01 shows backend query taking >20s then 504 from metrics service.
- Checked metrics ingestion (kafka -> metrics-service) around 2026-03-03 08:50-09:30 PST: small spike in consumer lag on metrics-consumer-2 (see monitoring alarm triggered at 08:58).

Hypotheses (prioritized):
1) Metrics ingestion lag caused partial/empty panels (prefix caching mismatch + stale series).
2) A query plan change in the metrics service made some long-running PromQL/SQL queries time out for heavy cardinality panels (model_id + route + region).
3) Rollout changed model tags; backend filter -> no matching series for some panels (easy to check).
4) Frontend bug: missing fallback when panels return empty + mis-handled error -> 500 surfaced to user.

Actions taken so far:
- Opened JIRA-4783 to track backend investigation (assigned to Jordan).
- Pinged metrics infra on #infra-observability (Maya) to check consumer lags and retention (done 2026-03-03 12:05 PST).
- Added short-term dashboard workaround: change queries to include OR on fallback metric (see temp panel edits) - not committed to main dashboard yet (need review).
- Collected logs and traces, attached to JIRA-4782 (customer-visible) and JIRA-4783 (internal).

Notes from Jordan (2026-03-03):
- Reproduced long query times on metrics-service v2.4.1; dev profiling shows heavy GC on instances with >10k series scans. Suspect a regression introduced in v2.4.1 query planner.
- Rollback option: metrics-service v2.4.0 can be rolled back in staging; need approval for canary rollback in prod.

Temporary mitigations (short term):
- Add try/catch + more informative error UI on panel (FE) so the customer sees "metrics timeout - partial data may be available" instead of raw 500. (Owner: FE team - tentative PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/456)
- Create a reduced-cardinality version of the slow panels (aggregate by model_family rather than model_id). This should reduce query scan cost. (Owner: me / Jordan)
- If ingestion lag persists, increase consumer group parallelism by +1 for metrics-consumer-2 (infra owner: Maya).

Outstanding questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm whether the model rollout changed tags/labels used by dashboards. (Owner: Nick) - quick grep of latest model metadata mapping scheduled.
- [ ] Decide on rollback of metrics-service v2.4.1 or patch. (Owner: Jordan, due 2026-03-04 EOD)
- [ ] Frontend error handling PR to replace 500 with user-friendly message and Sentry breadcrumb. (Owner: FE lead, cc @maya)
- [ ] Notify customer with status update + ETA. (Owner: CSM, but I'll draft message)
- [ ] Add automated smoke query for heavy-cardinality panels to detect regressions in canary. (Owner: SRE / observability)

Draft status update for customer (to be reviewed by CSM):
"Hi Team - quick update: We're investigating reports of missing panels and intermittent errors on the Model Latency dashboard. Early indications point to a metrics backend query regression that can cause timeouts for high-cardinality queries. We've opened internal ticket JIRA-4783 and are testing mitigations including a reduced-cardinality panel and enhanced frontend error messaging. Our next update by EOD PT. - Nick (observability)"

Quick checklist / timeline (my personal):
- 2026-03-03 11:00-13:00: triage, reproduce, collect logs - done.
- 2026-03-03 14:00: sync with Jordan + Maya - done.
- 2026-03-03 16:00: push temp panel with aggregated queries (staging) - in progress.
- 2026-03-04 09:00: decision on rollback vs patch - TODO.

Notes & debugging commands (for reference):
- grep model tag mappings: git grep "model_tag_map" -- console-dashboards/
- run heavy query locally: python tools/run_query.py --panel latency-by-model --start -1h --end now --limit 50000
- check consumer lag: kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --describe --group metrics-consumer-2
- tail metrics-service logs: kubectl -n observability logs -l app=metrics-service -c worker --since=2h | grep "query_time" | sort -r

Slack threads / refs:
- #console-observability thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C04OBSERV/ (search "Acme latency dashboard")
- Customer thread (via CSM): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/JIRA-4782

Decisions needed from infra/product today:
- Approve canary rollback of metrics-service to v2.4.0 (risk: masks underlying regression but buys time).
- Approve short-term aggregated panels change to dashboards (low risk).

Misc notes / ideas:
- Could add a per-customer panel namespace so dashboards automatically fall back to lower-cardinality aggregates when series count > X. Might be a good product improvement for Dedicated customers.
- Consider adding a synthetic monitor that queries each critical dashboard panel every 5m and alerts when >30% of panels are empty or erroring for an org.

Next actions (today):
- Finish aggregated-panel PR to staging and run smoke queries (Owner: Nick)
- Jordan to provide profiling artifact and rollback recommendation (Owner: Jordan)
- Maya to check consumer parallelism and confirm if increasing helps (Owner: Maya)
- Draft and send customer update after internal decision (Owner: Nick / CSM)

Notes-to-self: keep this doc as the single-source-of-notes for follow-ups; copy important links to JIRA-4783 so nothing gets lost.

Attachments (local): screenshots/, traces/, profiling/ (will upload to JIRA once cleaned)

---
2026-03-04 morning quick check: staging aggregated panels look ok, query runtime dropped from ~12s -> ~700ms for sample org. Need prod canary to validate.

End of scratchpad entry.
